name: Antichain Number of Quadratic-Residue Tournament Classes
proof: For the tournament class $\mathcal Q_p=\{C_a:a\in\mathbb F_p\}$, assign $C_a$ its consistent singleton sample at coordinate $a$. For distinct $a,b$, the two singleton samples are distinct, hence incomparable, so this is an antichain teacher mapping of width one. Since $p>1$, width zero would assign the same empty sample to two targets and violate the antichain condition. Thus $\mathrm{AN}(\mathcal Q_p)=1$.
references: Direct calculation from the tournament-class definition in \cite{simon2023tournaments}.
